title: GPU capacity bottleneck synthesis and regional mitigation — weekly log
content:
Date: 2029-09-18
Author: Marisol Chen (gpu-ops lead)
Purpose: Weekly synthesis of observed GPU bottlenecks across regions, quick triage notes from this week's standups, and concrete mitigation options for the next sprint.

Attendees (standup / sync): Devon, Riya, Liam, Beatrice, Tomas (SRE), Claire (Platform Eng), + four rotating ops engineers.

TL;DR:
- We observed three distinct bottleneck patterns this week: (A) short high-QPS spikes saturating KV-cache memory on p4d clusters (us-west1), (B) prolonged scheduling backpressure in apac-southeast1 tied to instance preemption and node churn, and (C) intermittent model-variant cold starts causing latency cliffs in europe-west3.
- Immediate mitigations (short window): bump regional buffer targets, enable conservative hedging to quantized-compatible variants for best-effort requests, extend prewarm window for high-risk model routes.
- Mid-term: test lightweight instance families in apac to reduce preemption sensitivity; add fine-grained queueing per-customer priority to prevent single-tenant storms.

Observations / Data points:
1) us-west1 spikes (2029-09-15 → 09-17)
   - Symptom: transient token-level latency increase from 60ms baseline → 420ms P95 for 2–3 minutes during several spikes.
   - Root indicator: KV cache invalidation churn correlated with large multi-message chat sessions; memory pressure on p4d_8 caused eviction cascades.
   - Measured: cache eviction rate ~3x baseline during spikes; per-node GPU memory pressure hit 92% on affected hosts.
   - Short-term fix applied: reduced per-request max_seq_len on non-priority routes; raised cache_retention to favor recent prefixes.

2) apac-southeast1 scheduling/backpressure (2029-09-16 → ongoing)
   - Symptom: instance preemption events rose 2.4x after cloud provider rebalancing; scheduling queue latency increased, causing backlog and request timeouts (~0.6% of total requests).
   - Constraint: limited access to non-preemptible pool in region; reserved capacity commit under discussion for Q4.
   - Impact: estimated 7% drop in sustained throughput for Dedicated customers on that region during peak windows.
   - Workaround: moved non-critical routes to nearby apac-edge POPs with lower concurrency profiles; enabling opportunistic burst in intra-region fallback policy.

3) europe-west3 model-variant cold starts (2029-09-14 → 09-18)
   - Symptom: new model rollout (quantized-7b-v2) exhibited occasional kernel selection stalls at scale leading to 1–2s latency spikes for first few requests after idle periods.
   - Hypothesis: compilation cache misses + non-optimal kernel selection for mixed sequence lengths.
   - Experiment: pinned a small canary pool with precompiled kernels and disabled on-demand kernel compilation for that canary; early results show P95 down from 1.2s → 240ms for canary traffic.

Synthesis / Root causes (why these patterns keep recurring):
- Workload variance: chat sessions with long prefixes are increasing KV cache pressure beyond current heuristics. Batching heuristics are tuned for median token lengths, not long-tail session length.
- Instance mix fragility: apac region has higher share of preemptible capacity in our fleet mix which makes us more vulnerable to provider rebalances.
- Model onboarding friction: new quantized variants sometimes require tailored kernel/compilation profiles when introduced; automation to detect and precompile per-region is incomplete.

Immediate action items (next 7 days):
- A1: Increase regional buffer target from 10% → 16% in apac-southeast1 for next 48h (owner: Devon) — JIRA INFRA-4857.
- A2: Roll hedging policy to allow automatic fallback to quantized-compatible variants for best-effort routes (owner: Riya) — rollout flag + canary at 10%.
- A3: Schedule a short lived "priming wave" for europe-west3 canary pool to build kernel caches pre-emptively on release nights (owner: Liam) — add to release checklist PR #2142.
- A4: Add KV cache pressure alert with a short-window derivative trigger (owner: Beatrice) — alert rule proposal in #gpu-ops.
- A5: Cost check: estimate 72-hour buffer bump cost delta for apac and get sign-off from finance if > $14k (owner: Marisol).

Mid-term proposals (2–6 weeks):
- M1: Fleet diversity pilot in apac — test a mix of smaller GPU families (gn6a-like) for low-latency interactive workloads to reduce preemption sensitivity. Prepare A/B experiment with 5% traffic.
- M2: Session-length-aware batching — modify batching controller to partition by predicted remaining sequence length to avoid KV cache evictions caused by merging extremely long sessions with short sessions.
- M3: Per-route priming policy — add route-level priming windows that prewarm kernels and KV caches ahead of expected peak windows (based on past 30d traffic profile).

Open questions / Risks:
- Q1: If we increase buffer targets globally, what is the sustained cost impact vs. customer SLA benefit? Need a simple model to trade off cost → latency SLO improvements.
- Q2: How quickly can finance sign-off on a temporary regional buffer cost? If delayed, we may have to rely exclusively on hedging and priming which are less effective for some classes of traffic.
- Q3: Are there non-cloud-provider mitigations (e.g., smarter eviction policies or multi-tenant isolation) that can be implemented without additional spend?

Meeting notes / quick logs (chronological):
- 09-15 09:05: Spike captured by synthetic-runner (tag: long-prefix-chat). Detailed traces pushed to INFRA-4789.
- 09-16 11:20: apac preemption wave observed; on-call rotated and applied fallback rules.
- 09-17 02:00: night priming test for europe-west3; canary precompile script executed (success: 96% precompile hit).
- 09-18 08:30: engineering triage — agreed to A1..A5 and mid-term M1..M3 list.

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep record of any customer complaints routed to CS about latency during these windows. I want a mapping of customer-id → route → approx-latency degradation to discuss at next PS call.
- We should consider a small internal playbook: "if KV cache eviction rate > X AND apu_util% > Y then scale ephemeral pool by Z". This could buy us minutes during spikes.

Appendix (quick metrics snapshot):
- Global P95 baseline (token-latency): 68ms.
- us-west1 peak spike P95: 420ms (duration: ~2–3m x 4 events).
- apac-southeast1 preemption rate: 0.9% → 2.2% (week-over-week).
- europe-west3 cold-start P95 (before priming): 1.2s; canary after priming: 240ms.

Action ownership summary (single-line):
- Devon: regional buffer bump (A1) — INFRA-4857.
- Riya: hedging policy rollout (A2) — feature-flag.
- Liam: canary priming schedule & scripts (A3) — PR #2142.
- Beatrice: KV cache pressure alert; dashboard (A4).
- Marisol: finance cost check and exec note (A5).

If you have updates, drop them in the #gpu-ops thread and tag owners. Will re-sync mid-week if any of the A items escalate.

-- end of log
